The difference formula for cosine gives

$$
\begin{aligned}R\operatorname{cos}⁡(x-ϕ) & =R(\operatorname{cos}⁡x\operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ+\operatorname{sin}⁡x\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ) \\  & =R\operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ\operatorname{cos}⁡x+R\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ\operatorname{sin}⁡x.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, by writing the given expression in the amplitude-phase form

$$
\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡x+\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡x=R\operatorname{cos}⁡(x-ϕ),
$$

we get the following identity:

$$
\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡x+\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡x=(R\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ)\operatorname{sin}⁡x+(R\operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ)\operatorname{cos}⁡x
$$

 

Equating the coefficients of $\operatorname{sin}⁡x$ and $\operatorname{cos}⁡x,$ we get the following system of equations:

$$
\{\begin{aligned}R\operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ=\frac{1}{2} \\ R\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ=\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Dividing the second equation by the first, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{R\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ}{R\operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ} & =\frac{(\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2})}{(\frac{1}{2})} \\ \operatorname{tan}⁡ϕ & =\sqrt{3} \\ ϕ & =\operatorname{arctan}⁡(\sqrt{3}) \\ ϕ & =\frac{\pi }{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we find the amplitude $R.$ Squaring the first and the second equations of the system and adding the results together, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{(R\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ)}^{2}+{(R\operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ)}^{2} & ={(\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2})}^{2}+{(\frac{1}{2})}^{2} \\ {R}^{2}({sin}^{2}⁡ϕ+{cos}^{2}⁡ϕ) & =\frac{3}{4}+\frac{1}{4} \\ {R}^{2} & =1 \\ R & =1.\end{aligned}
$$

 

Note that we only consider the positive root since $R>0.$

Finally, we can write the initial expression in amplitude-phase form as follows:

$$
\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡x+\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡x=\operatorname{cos}⁡(x-\frac{\pi }{3})
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}R\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x-ϕ) & =R(\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x)\operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ-\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x)\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ) \\  & =R\operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x)-R\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x)\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, by writing the given expression in the amplitude-phase form

$$
4\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x)-10\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x)=R\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x-ϕ),
$$

we get the following identity:

$$
4\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x)-10\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x)=(R\operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ)\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x)-(R\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ)\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x)
$$

Equating the coefficients of $\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x)$ and $\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x),$ we get the following system of equations:

$$
\{\begin{aligned}R\operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ=4 \\ R\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ=10\end{aligned}
$$

Dividing the second equation by the first, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{R\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ}{R\operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ} & =\frac{10}{4} \\ \operatorname{tan}⁡ϕ & =\frac{5}{2} \\ ϕ & =\operatorname{arctan}⁡(\frac{5}{2}).\end{aligned}
$$

$$

Therefore, by writing the given expression in the amplitude-phase form

$$
3\operatorname{sin}⁡x-4\operatorname{cos}⁡x=R\operatorname{sin}⁡(x-ϕ),
$$

we get the following identity:

$$
3\operatorname{sin}⁡x-4\operatorname{cos}⁡x=(R\operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ)\operatorname{sin}⁡x-(R\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ)\operatorname{cos}⁡x
$$

Equating the coefficients of $\operatorname{sin}⁡x$ and $\operatorname{cos}⁡x,$ we get the following system of equations:

$$
\{\begin{aligned}R\operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ=3 \\ R\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ=4\end{aligned}
$$

Dividing the second equation by the first, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{R\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ}{R\operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ} & =\frac{4}{3} \\ \operatorname{tan}⁡ϕ & =\frac{4}{3} \\ ϕ & =\operatorname{arctan}⁡(\frac{4}{3}) \\  & ≈0.927\,\text{rad}\end{aligned}
$$

rounded to three decimal places.

Now, we find the amplitude $R.$ Squaring the first and the second equations of the system and adding the results together, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{(R\operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ)}^{2}+{(R\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ)}^{2} & =(3)^{2}+(4)^{2} \\ {R}^{2}({cos}^{2}⁡ϕ+{sin}^{2}⁡ϕ) & =9+16 \\ {R}^{2} & =25 \\ R & =5.\end{aligned}
$$

Note that we only consider the positive root since $R>0.$

$$
3\operatorname{sin}⁡x-4\operatorname{cos}⁡x≈5\operatorname{sin}⁡(x-0.927)
$$
